subject: AWS Marketplace commercial exception: CloudRetail - commission & payment term request
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia@cloudretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finance - CloudRetail <finance@cloudretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Special commission & payment terms for AWS Marketplace private listing - CloudRetail

Hi Irene + Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. CloudRetail is ready to move forward with an AWS Marketplace private listing but we hit two blockers on our procurement side that need commercial exception:

- Rev-share: AWS requires we agree a listing commission structure; our procurement is asking for a 25% revenue share to accommodate reseller margins (your standard cap is 15%).
- Payment terms: we need Net90 for the first 9 months to align cashflow with our vendor contracts.

Attached is our SOW and a 12-month usage forecast to help model economics. The ask is one-time: elevated rev-share for the first 12 months and Net90; after that we revert to standard 15% and Net30.

Can your team advise on whether Redwood can approve a one-time commercial exception and what governance we need (finance holdback, clawback language, etc.)? AWS PM also flagged potential eligibility gating.

Appreciate quick guidance — procurement needs this confirmed by 11/06 to meet their quarter close.

Best,
Olivia

Attachments: CloudRetail_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF), Usage_Forecast.xlsx (Excel)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Special commission & payment terms for AWS Marketplace private listing - CloudRetail

Karthik — looping in Deal Desk (Marissa) and revenue ops for quick triage.

High-level read: 25% rev-share and Net90 are both outside standard policy. We can consider a limited-duration exception if we 1) cap total uplift to a dollar threshold, 2) add a finance holdback / clawback for overpayments, and 3) require AWS confirmation of listing eligibility.

Please review the forecast and give me a recommended escalation ask (exact uplift %, term length, and financial guardrails). I want a concise executive note to take to revenue leadership by EOD 11/03.

Irene
VP, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-02T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Special commission & payment terms for AWS Marketplace private listing - CloudRetail

Irene / Marissa,

Reviewed the attachments and ran preliminary economics against the standard 15% baseline. Key points:

- 25% rev-share at forecasted volume would exceed our typical acquisition CAC allowance and reduce Redwood margin considerably. We should not accept full 25% unless there's a spend guarantee or significant upfront.
- Net90 materially increases collections risk; finance will require a holdback or 10% reserve for the first 6 months.

Recommendation (deal desk):
1) Offer a bridging structure: 20% rev-share for first 6 months + a $200k upfront credit/guarantee from CloudRetail (applied to rev-share overage).
2) Approve Net60 instead of Net90; if Finance insists on Net90, require a 12% holdback and a clawback clause tied to actual invoiced vs. paid.
3) Executive approval required for any uplift over 18% or payment terms beyond Net60. Please escalate to revenue lead with these options.

Deal ID: DL-2026-4489
Link: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/4489

-karthik
Senior Deal Desk Manager

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-03T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: executive clearance — CloudRetail commercial exception (summary & ask)

Jonas — quick ask for executive clearance. Background and proposed guardrails below; happy to jump on 15m if helpful.

Summary:
- Account: CloudRetail Inc. (Retail SaaS) — forecasted first-year ARR $4.8M on AWS marketplace listing.
- External ask: 25% rev-share for 12 months + Net90 for first 9 months.

Deal Desk recommendation (option A, preferred):
- Approve 20% rev-share for first 6 months only; revert to standard 15% thereafter.
- Require $200k upfront guarantee or credit to offset margin impact.
- Approve Net60; Finance to hold 12% of invoices for first 6 months as reserve.
- Include a 12-month clawback if revenue goals not met (pro-rated).
- Limit approval to up to $1.2M in Redwood revenue impact (beyond which a renewed sign-off is required).

Why: balances probability of closing with acceptable economics and risk controls. If CloudRetail refuses Net60, we would need stronger upfront (50% of guarantee) or decline.

Ask: Jonas, please confirm executive clearance to proceed with Deal Desk option A or indicate any modifications. Need decision by EOD 11/05 to meet CloudRetail timeline.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CR_approval_memo.pdf (internal memo)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-05T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: executive clearance — CloudRetail commercial exception (summary & ask)

Marissa / team,

Thanks for the crisp write-up. Approve Deal Desk option A with the following non-negotiable conditions:

1) Approval limited to a maximum Redwood revenue impact of $1.2M (first 12 months). If CloudRetail's actual billed amount exceeds that, we revert to standard terms unless I re-sign.
2) Finance to implement a 12% holdback for invoices during the first 6 months; holdback to be released pro-rata once collections are confirmed.
3) Legal to add a clawback clause and explicit audit rights; SOC2 report required from CloudRetail prior to listing.
4) Require AWS Marketplace PM confirmation in writing that the private listing is eligible under their policies.

Irene — please coordinate with finance and legal to draft the term sheet and send a single-page executive summary back to me before you present to CloudRetail.

Jonas Weber
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
